issues.move: Excluding Romans 8:28 and Jeremiah 29:11 from the crisis surface as "explanation verses" under negative religious coping
issues.problem: The design cites persona-research.md:139 as the evidential basis for excluding these two verses, but that line's actual taxonomy contradicts the exclusion. Line 139 reads: 'Positive religious coping (God's presence, benevolent reframing), which predicts better outcomes; negative coping ("punishing God", "have more faith") predicts decline (Pargament & Koenig 2004, longitudinal).' Romans 8:28 ('God works all things together for good') is a textbook instance of benevolent reframing, which the research explicitly places in the POSITIVE coping bucket, not the negative one. Negative coping in the cited research is defined by content like a punishing God or demands for more faith — neither of which matches Romans 8:28 or Jeremiah 29:11 ('plans to prosper you'). The design invents a new category ('explanation verses') that appears nowhere in the research document and maps it onto the Pargament citation backwards.
issues.evidence: docs/PERSONA-RESEARCH-2026-09-10.md:139 (present on branch docs/persona-research-2026-09-10, not on main) — 'Positive religious coping (God's presence, benevolent reframing)...predicts better outcomes; negative coping ("punishing God", "have more faith") predicts decline.' Compare to the design's principles list: 'Romans 8:28 and Jeremiah 29:11 are explanation verses and are excluded from the crisis surface (Pargament: negative religious coping predicts decline)' and the evidence-array entry citing the same line-139 quote as support for the exclusion.
issues.fix: Either drop the Pargament citation for this specific move and justify the exclusion on pastoral/editorial grounds alone (a legitimate call Ashley can make), or reclassify honestly: the research's own taxonomy would place 'God works all things for good' under benevolent reframing/positive coping, so citing Pargament as the reason to REMOVE it misstates the source. State in open_decisions that this exclusion is a design judgment, not a research-sourced one.
